description:
Goal
After fz-hwn.19.2 has made artifact-owned callable entries and boundary contracts read TransportPlan facts, cut downstream callable materialization over to that inventory. Native/interpreter/backend consumers may materialize closures or callable boundaries only when the artifact handoff names the required CallableId or BoundaryId.

Why
Callable entries and published boundary contracts are artifact products after the transport/artifact seam. Downstream code must not rediscover them from function plus capture types, all callable-looking producers, local shape evidence, or native closure-construction scans.

Required changes
Native boundaries, identity fns, closure allocation, callable-boundary arguments, and first-class publication read the artifact/TransportPlan-backed CallableId and BoundaryId inventory produced by fz-hwn.19.2. Direct callable transport reads CallableId target and capture facts. First-class materialization reads the attached BoundaryId contract. Codegen/native lowering must never re-select a boundary from capture count, capture types, or all MakeClosure/MakeFnRef sites.

Removal target
Native callable boundary selection from capture types as authority, broad callable-looking type recovery, settled_callable_boundary lookup by local shape, native callable identity collection from all callable producers, callable object materialization without a BoundaryId fact, and any downstream path that publishes a callable entry instead of consuming the artifact inventory.

Checks
Unused callable constructor publishes no downstream materialization; direct lambda call stays direct; direct callable crosses return/resume without heap closure; escaped lambda materializes exactly the BoundaryId named by artifact; opaque callable path has explicit BoundaryId contract. Any remaining fz-hwn.13 symptom must be blocked by a separate non-transport bug ticket with evidence.

comments.text:
VERIFIED AGAINST HEAD (ticket partly stale). Findings:
1. Designated contract test compiler2_native_codegen_materializes_the_settled_callable_boundary_for_opaque_closures pins a PROVABLY WRONG invariant: its fixture (closure_typed_captures.fz) is a DIRECT callable (transport: direct=1, boundary_pub=0), not an opaque boundary. compiler2 resolves f.(x) directly. The test must be repointed to assert direct dispatch (proposal §10.1).
2. native_codegen/prim.rs::settled_callable_boundary_id is NOT a disease site — it only READS the pre-tagged callable_value_boundaries. No capture-type selection there.
3. The ONLY capture-type-selection disease is jobs/native.rs::select_settled_callable_boundary, called once at materialize_transport_value (the rematerialize-callable-from-lanes site). Empirically (whole-suite probe) it is BEHAVIOR-INVARIANT: every reachable materialized callable has exactly ONE boundary_id and capture-type selection already equals the CallableId fact. Its widest/min-var tie-break is dead in practice.
4. The aggravating multi-surface case (one callable, two surfaces, escaped) produces multiple boundaries but does NOT reach that site — escaped 0-cap callables materialize as static closure singletons in the codegen driver (emit_callable_boundary_bodies/fetch_static_closure), a path steeped in TrashDeliveredShape/ArgRepr = fz-hwn.19.5 territory.

RE-SCOPE: (a) cut materialize_transport_value over to read the CallableId->boundary_ids fact and DELETE select_settled_callable_boundary (correct-by-construction, removes the latent mis-pick surface; behavior-invariant today). (b) Fix the old-world test to assert direct dispatch. (c) The escaped/multi-surface boundary selection (static-singleton driver path) is fz-hwn.19.5 scope — recorded so it is not done out-of-layer.

title: Transport cutover: make downstream callable materialization consume artifact BoundaryId inventory
